title: A Landfall for the Wreck
premise: When a government survey team vanishes in the highlands, leaving their gear stacked neatly and no tracks behind, Vesper Joubert is the only person both willing and able to go looking. Following a river upstream toward its forbidden source, he uncovers his late father's hidden excavation and learns the vanished team found something worth killing to keep buried. Betrayed by the one ally he trusted, Vesper must choose between exposing the truth that destroyed his family or protecting the ragtag crew who became his real inheritance. He chooses truth, survives the monsoon's landfall by flooding the site forever, and comes home at last—not to a place, but to people.
about_author: Oscar Sandoval is a former river guide turned novelist who has spent two decades paddling waterways most maps refuse to name. His fiction draws on the drowned villages, sealed archives, and stubborn locals he met along the way.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Working a routine contract survey on the coast, Vesper measures his life in distance traveled rather than time lived, still estranged from his dead father's legacy. A government telegram arrives: a survey team has vanished upstream, and they want him because he's 'the better digger.' Emotional beat: restless loneliness cracked open by an unwelcome summons.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the abandoned campsite he finds the team's equipment arranged with eerie care—boots paired, journals weighted shut—and not a single footprint leading away. The last journal page names his father's old dig coordinates. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Crew Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with interludes from ferry-woman Maren. Vesper assembles a found-family crew: Maren, ex-soldier Tull, and teenage tracker Ivo, each running from something. They sign on for money but stay for reasons they won't say aloud. Emotional beat: wary bonds forming over shared firelight and unspoken debts.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Tull's POV. The river narrows into country where maps go blank and local law outranks government paper. An elder warns them the source is forbidden and offers them one night's shelter, no more. Vesper finds his father's initials carved in stone, decades old. Emotional beat: humility before a landscape that owes nothing to outsiders.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The tracker discovers a drowned village beneath a clear pool—roof beams, a church bell, and modern rope among ancient stones. Someone has been diving here recently. The gear matches the missing survey team. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear; the vanishing was no accident of terrain.

chapters.title: The Father's Vault
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Above the source, hidden behind a waterfall, Vesper finds his father's final excavation: a sealed chamber of artifacts proving the government knowingly flooded the valley and falsified its history. His father died protecting it. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into fury; inheritance finally understood.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The survey team's sole survivor emerges—a broken cartographer who reveals the expedition leader sold out to officials who want the chamber destroyed and everyone who saw it silenced. One of Vesper's own crew has been reporting their position. Emotional beat: betrayal landing like a physical blow; loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Storm clouds swallow the ridge as the traitor's handlers arrive by helicopter. Vesper must document everything before the rains hit, while Tull holds the trail and Maren readies the boat. Emotional beat: desperate clarity—the choice between safety and truth can no longer be deferred.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Full-crew POV rotation during the climax. In the storm's first assault, Vesper floods the chamber deliberately, sealing the valley's secret in rising water while broadcasting copies of the evidence downstream. The traitor, offered escape, chooses instead to hold the pass and redeem himself. Emotional beat: sacrifice, fury, and release as the monsoon erases the battlefield.

chapters.title: The Better Digger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Weeks later, the evidence forces an inquiry; the drowned village will be memorialized, not erased. Vesper turns down a prestigious post and instead signs on with Maren's ferry run, with Ivo apprenticed beside him. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—he stops measuring life in miles and starts measuring it in the people who stayed.
